Rep. Lloyd Smucker addresses Medicaid fraud and celebrates York County anniversary
Rep. Lloyd Smucker, U.S. Congressman representing Pennsylvania’s 11th district since 2017, recently used his social media platform to address Medicaid fraud, community engagement with local students, and the history of York County.
On August 17, 2026, Smucker highlighted concerns about misuse of public funds in healthcare programs: "Medicaid provides critical support to Americans who truly need it. Every dollar stolen through fraud is a dollar taken away from the individuals who rely on these programs—and from hardworking taxpayers. I spoke with Fox News about the disturbing Medicaid fraud allegations here".
A day later, on August 18, Smucker shared details of his visit to Franklin & Marshall College: "Enjoyed a great visit at Franklin & Marshall College with President Andy Rich, and F&M Board of Trustees Vice Chair and alumnus Ken Mehlman. Appreciated a great discussion with students about leadership, resilience, and the lessons we've learned throughout our careers."
On August 19, he marked an important milestone for York County: "On this day in 1749, York County was founded. For 277 years, generations of hardworking Pennsylvanians have called York County home and contributed to its rich history and strong communities. Happy Birthday, York County!"
Lloyd Smucker has served as U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 11th District since succeeding Joe Pitts in 2017. Before joining Congress, he represented his region in the Pennsylvania Senate from 2009 to 2016. Born in Lancaster County in 1964 and currently residing there at age 59, Smucker continues to engage both local constituents and national audiences on policy issues affecting Pennsylvania.
